subject: aerospace-engineering
intro: Aerospace engineering leads to the teams that put vehicles into the sky and keep them there — shaping aircraft and spacecraft, proving their structures, powering them and flying them safely.

roles.title: Aerospace Engineers
roles.what: Perform engineering duties in designing, constructing and testing aircraft, missiles and spacecraft, conduct research on how materials and equipment adapt to flight, and recommend improvements in testing equipment and techniques.
roles.where: The whole arc applies: aerodynamics and compressible flow for shapes, structures and fatigue for airframes, propulsion for thrust, flight mechanics and control for handling, and orbital mechanics for the spacecraft half of the job.

roles.title: Aerospace Engineering and Operations Technologists and Technicians
roles.what: Operate, install, adjust and maintain the computer and communications systems, consoles, simulators and test instruments used to launch, track, position and evaluate air and space vehicles, recording and interpreting test data.
roles.where: Flight control and avionics — sensors, navigation, autopilot loops — and the measurement mindset from the testing strand prepare you to run the ground and flight test equipment this role operates every day.

roles.title: Avionics Technicians
roles.what: Install, inspect, test, adjust or repair avionics equipment — radar, radio, navigation and missile control systems — in aircraft or space vehicles.
roles.where: The flight control and avionics unit — fly-by-wire, autopilot loops, navigation and sensors — plus modulation and noise from the communications strand give you the system knowledge this job installs and repairs.

roles.title: Aircraft Mechanics and Service Technicians
roles.what: Diagnose, adjust, repair or overhaul aircraft engines and assemblies, such as hydraulic and pneumatic systems, keeping airframes and powerplants safe and airworthy.
roles.where: Propulsion — turbojets, turbofans and turboprops — aerospace structures with fatigue and composites, and certification and airworthiness from the design unit are exactly the systems and rules you maintain.
